questions.question: The average weight of P and his three friends is 55 kg. If P is 4 kg more than the average weight of his three friends, what is P's weight (in kg)?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total weight of P and his 3 friends = 4 × 55 = 220 kg.

Let P's weight be P. The average of the 3 friends is (P − 4) kg.

Total weight = P + 3 × (P − 4) = 220

⇒ 4P − 12 = 220

⇒ 4P = 232 ⇒ P = 58 kg.

**∴ The correct answer is 58 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Average weight of P and his 3 friends = 55 kg

P's weight is 4 kg more than the average weight of his 3 friends.

**Formula Used:**

Sum of values = Average × Number of values

 Average of 4 persons = 55 kg
 
 
 3 Friends
 Total Weight = 3x

 
 Person P
 Weight = x + 4

 

 Total Weight = 4 × 55 = 220 kg

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the average weight of the 3 friends be x kg.

⇒ Total weight of the 3 friends = 3x kg

⇒ Weight of P = (x + 4) kg

⇒ Total weight of all 4 persons = 4 × 55 = 220 kg

⇒ 3x + (x + 4) = 220

⇒ 4x + 4 = 220

⇒ 4x = 216

⇒ x = 216 ÷ 4 = 54 kg

⇒ P's weight = x + 4 = 54 + 4 = 58 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 58 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Basic Average

Average = Sum of all observations ÷ Total number of observations.

Weighted Average

If two groups have sizes n₁ and n₂ with averages A₁ and A₂, Combined Average = (n₁ × A₁ + n₂ × A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).

Net Deviation Method

The sum of deviations of all individual values from their average is always zero. This property helps in finding an unknown observation quickly.
</p

questions.question: A sold a mobile phone to B at a gain of 25% and B sold it to C at a loss of 10%. If C paid Rs. 5,625 for it, how much did A pay (in Rs.) for the phone?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A sold a mobile phone to B at a gain of 25%

B sold the mobile to C at a loss of 10%

Total money paid by C = Rs. 5625

**Calculation:**

Let, the A paid for the mobile phone = x

So, x × (125/100) × (90/100) = 5625

⇒ x = 5625 × (100/125) × (100/90)

⇒ x = 5000

**∴ A paid Rs. 5000 (in Rs.) for the phone**

questions.question: A motorboat whose speed is 20 km/h in still water takes 30 minutes more to go 24 km upstream than to cover the same distance downstream. If the speed of the boat in still water is increased by 2 km/h, then how much time will it take to go 39 km downstream and 30 km upstream?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The speed of the motorboat in still water = 20 km/h

**Concept used:**

If the speed of a boat in still water is x km/h and the speed of the stream is y km/h, then

Downstream speed = (x + y) km/h

Upstream speed = (x - y) km/h

Time = Distance/Speed

**Calculation:**

According to the question, the motorboat takes 30 minutes more to go 24 km upstream than to cover the same distance downstream.

Let, the speed of the water = x km/h

So, 24/(20 - x) = 24/(20 + x) + (1/2) [∵ 30 minutes = 1/2 hour]

⇒ 24/(20 - x) - 24/(20 + x) = (1/2)

⇒ (24(20+x)-24(20-x))/(400-x²)=(1)/(2)

⇒ (24(20+x-20+x))/(400-x²)=(1)/(2)

⇒ (24×2x)/(400-x²)=(1)/(2)

⇒ 400 - x² = 96x

⇒ x² + 96x - 400 = 0

⇒ x2 + 100x - 4x - 400 = 0

⇒ x (x + 100) - 4 (x + 100) = 0

⇒ (x + 100) (x - 4) = 0

⇒ x + 100 = 0 ⇒ x = -100 ["-" is neglacted]

⇒ x - 4 = 0 ⇒ x = 4

∴ The speed of the water = 4 km/h

The speed of the motorboat in still water increased 2 km/h = 20 + 2 = 22 km/h

The time for 39 km downstream and 30 km upstream = 39/(22 + 4) + 30/(22 - 4) hours

= (39/26) + (30/18) hours

= 3/2 + 5/3 hours

= 19/6 hours

= (19/6) × 60 minutes

= 190 minutes

= 3 hours 10 minutes

**∴ The motorboat will take 3 hours 10 minutes to go 39 km downstream and 30 km upstream**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__**Value putting method, 

According to the question, 

30 min = 1/2 hr

x = 20 (Speed in still water)

⇒ 24/(20 - y) - 24/(20 + y) = 1/2

Here the R.H.S is 1/2, so the value of 20 - y must be more than 12

Hence take y = 4 (so that right bracket will become 1 as 20 + 4 = 24) and (left bracket will be more than half)

⇒ 24/(20 - 4) - 24(20 + 4) = 3/2 - 1 = 1/2

Hence the value of Y = 4

Now according to the question, 

⇒ 39/(22 + 4) + 30/(22 - 4) = 39/26 + 30/18

⇒ 19/6 = 3(1/6) = 3 hours and 10 min

∴ The motorboat will take 3 hours 10 minutes to go 39 km downstream and 30 km upstream

questions.question: Find the greatest number 23a68b, which is divisible by 3 but NOT divisible by 9.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The given number = 23a68b

**Concept used:**

**Divisibility rule of 3:** A number will be divisible by 3 if the sum of the digits of the number is divisible by 3

**Divisibility rule of 9:** A number will be divisible by 9 if the sum of the digits of the number is divisible by 9

**Calculation:**

For option 1, the sum of the digits = 2 + 3 + 8 + 6 + 8 + 9 = 36 (Divisible by 3 and 9)

For option 2, the sum of the digits = 2 + 3 + 9 + 6 + 8 + 5 = 33 (Divisible by 3 but not divisible by 9)

For option 3, the sum of the digits = 2 + 3 + 9 + 6 + 8 + 8 = 36 (Divisible by 3 and 9)

For option 4, the sum of the digits = 2 + 3 + 7 + 6 + 8 + 7 = 33 (Divisible by 3 but not divisible by 9)

So, 239685 and 237687 are divisible by 3 but not divisible by 9

The greatest number among them = 239685

**∴ The greatest number is 239685 which is divisible by 3 but NOT divisible by 9**

questions.question: Some students (only boys and girls) from different schools appeared for an Olympiad exam. 20% of the boys and 15% of the girls failed the exam. The number of boys who passed the exam was 70 more than that of the girls who passed the exam. A total of 90 students failed. Find the number of students that appeared for the exam.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

20% of the boys and 15% of the girls failed the exam.

Total number of students who failed = 90

**Calculation:**

The percentage of boys who passed = (100 - 20)% = 80%

The percentage of girls who passed = (100 - 15)% = 85%

Let, the number of appeared boys = x

The number of appeared girls = y

So, 80x/100 - 85y/100 = 70

⇒ 5 (16x - 17y) = 7000

⇒ 16x - 17y = 1400 .....(1)

Also, 20x/100 + 15y/100 = 90

⇒ 5 (4x + 3y) = 9000

⇒ 4x + 3y = 1800 .....(2)

Multiplying 4 to equation (2),

16x + 12y = 7200 .....(3)

Subtracting equation (2) from equation (3),

16x + 12y - 16x + 17y = 7200 - 1400

⇒ 29y = 5800

⇒ y = 5800/29 = 200

∴ The number of girls appeared = 200

Putting y = 200 in equation (2),

4x + 3 × 200 = 1800

⇒ 4x = 1800 - 600 = 1200

⇒ x = 1200/4 = 300

∴ The number of boys who appeared = 300

The total number of students who appeared = 300 + 200 = 500

**∴ The number of students that appeared for the exam is 500**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] __Alternate Method__** Calculation:-

Let the Number of boys and Girls who appeared in exam be x and y respectively,

So, according to question-

Number of boys passed in exam = [(100 - 20) × x]/100 = 0.80x

Number of girls passed in exam = [(100 - 15) × y]/100 = 0.85y

__Condition__ (1) - 

⇒ 0.80x = 0.85y + 70

⇒ 0.80x - 0.85y = 70 ...(i)

__Condition__ (2) -

Total failed students = 90

⇒ 0.20x + 0.15y = 90 ...(ii)

From eqⁿ (1) - [4 × eqⁿ (ii)]

⇒ (-0.85y) - 0.60y = 70 - 360 

⇒ 1.45y = 290

⇒ y = 200

Put this value in eqⁿ (i)

⇒ 0.80x = 0.85 × 200 + 70

⇒ 0.80x = 170 + 70 = 240

⇒ x = 300

So, **total number of students appeared in exam = 300 + 200 = 500.**

questions.question: If (x + 6y) = 8, and xy = 2, where x > 0, what is the value of (x³ + 216y³)?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

(x + 6y) = 8

xy = 2

**Formula used:**

(a + b)³ = a³ + b³ + 3ab (a + b)

**Calculation:**

xy = 2

⇒ y = 2/x .....(1)

Also, (x + 6y) = 8

⇒ x + (6 × 2/x) = 8

⇒ x + 12/x = 8 .....(2)

⇒ (x + 12/x)³ = 8³ [Taking cube of both sides]

⇒ x³ + (12/x)³ + 3 × x × (12/x) (x + 12/x) = 512

⇒ x3 + (12/x)3 + 3 × 12 × 8 = 512 [∵ We get from equation (2), x + 12/x = 8]

⇒ x3 + (12/x)3 + 288 = 512

⇒ x3 + (12/x)3 = 512 - 288

⇒ x3 + [(2 × 6)/x]³ = 224

⇒ x3 + (6y)³ = 224 [∵ y = 2/x]

⇒ x3 + 216y³ = 224

**∴ The value of x3 + 216y3 is 224**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] __Alternate Method__**Using Formula - (a + b)3 = a3 + b3 + 3ab (a + b)

(x + 6y)³ = x³ + 216y³ + 3 × x × 6y(x + 6y)

Put (x + 6y) = 8, xy = 2

⇒ 8³ = x3 + 216y3 + 3 × 6 × 2 × 8

⇒ x3 + 216y3 = 512 - 288

⇒ x3 + 216y3 = 224

∴ The value of x3 + 216y3 is 224.

4a

questions.question: In a ΔABC, points P, Q and R are taken on AB, BC and CA, respectively, such that BQ = PQ and QC = QR. If ∠BAC = 75º, what is the measure of ∠PQR (in degrees)?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/626ab74d9ea5000cf727fc54c65f1619ee6984d00c3e11ea54b5c299b076fd9c.png] 

∠BAC = 75º

∠ABC + ∠ACB + ∠BAC = 180°

∠ABC + ∠ACB + 75° = 180°

∠ABC + ∠ACB = 180° - 75° = 105°

Let, ∠ABC = ∠PBQ = 70° and ∠ACB = ∠RCQ = 35°

So, ∠PQR = 180° - (∠PQB + ∠RQC)

= 180° - [(180° - 2∠PBQ) + (180° - 2∠RCQ) [∵ BQ = PQ; QC = QR]

= 180° - [(180° - 2 × 70°) + (180° - 2 × 35°)]

= 180° - (40° + 110°)

= 180° - 150°

= 30°

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

In a ΔABC, ∠BAC = 75º

BQ = PQ and QC = QR

**Concept used:**

The sum of all three angles of a triangle = 180°

The sum of all angles on a straight line = 180°

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/626ab74d9ea5000cf727fc54c65f1619ee6984d00c3e11ea54b5c299b076fd9c.png] 

Let, ∠ABC = x and ∠ACB = y

So, ∠ABC = ∠PBQ = ∠QPB = x [∵ BQ = PQ]

∠ACB = ∠RCQ = ∠QRC = y [QC = QR]

In ΔABC, ∠ABC + ∠ACB + ∠BAC = 180°

⇒ x + y + 75° = 180°

⇒ x + y = 180° - 75° = 105° .....(1)

For ΔBPQ and ΔCRQ,

(∠PBQ + ∠QPB + ∠PQB) + (∠RCQ + ∠QRC + ∠RQC) = 180° + 180° = 360°

⇒ (x + x + ∠PQB) + (y + y + ∠RQC) = 360°

⇒ 2x + 2y + ∠PQB + ∠RQC = 360°

⇒ 2 (x + y) + ∠PQB + ∠RQC = 360°

⇒ (2 × 105°) + ∠PQB + ∠RQC = 360° [∵ x + y = 105°]

⇒ ∠PQB + ∠RQC = 360° - 210° = 150° .....(2)

Also, ∠PQB + ∠RQC + ∠PQR = 180°

⇒ 150° + ∠PQR = 180° [∵ ∠PQB + ∠RQC = 150°]

⇒ ∠PQR = 180° - 150° = 30°

**∴ The measure of ∠PQR (in degrees) is 30°**

questions.question: A can finish a piece of the work in 16 days and B can finish it in 12 days. They worked together for 4 days and then A left. B finished the remaining work. For how many total number of days did B work to finish the work completely?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/22ee47dc490db05e3283359554e56bc9e58030a06d01c74c4d75aba7b11ef98a.png] 

Total work = 48 (LCM of 16 and 12)

Efficiency = Work/Time

Total efficiency = 3 + 4 = 7 units

Remaining work after 4 days = 48 - (7 × 4) = 48 - 28 = 20 units

Time is taken by B to finish the remaining work = 20/4 = 5 days

Total number of days B work = 4 + 5 = 9 days

∴ B work the total number 9 days to finish the work completely.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

A can finish a piece of the work in 16 days

B can finish the same work in 12 days

**Calculation:**

A can finish in 1 day = 1/16 work

A can finish in 4 days = 4/16 = 1/4 work

B can finish in 1 day = 1/12 work

B can finish in 4 days = 4/12 = 1/3 work

The remaining work = 1 - [(1/4) + (1/3)]

= 1 - (7/12)

= 5/12

Time taken by B to finish the work = (5/12) ÷ (1/12) = (5/12) × 12 = 5 days

Total number of days B work = 4 + 5 = 9 days

**∴ B work the total number 9 days to finish the work completely.**

questions.question: LCM of two numbers is 56 times their HCF, with the sum of their HCF and LCM being 1710. If one of the two numbers is 240, then what is the other number?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Given LCM = 56 × HCF and LCM + HCF = 1710.

Total parts = 56 + 1 = 57 parts = 1710 ⇒ 1 part (HCF) = 30.

LCM = 56 × 30 = 1680.

Using the property: First Number × Second Number = HCF × LCM

Other number = (30 × 1680) ÷ 240 = 210.

**∴ The correct answer is 210.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

LCM = 56 × HCF

LCM + HCF = 1710

One number (N₁) = 240

**Formula Used:**

LCM × HCF = N₁ × N₂

 
 Number 1 × Number 2
 240 × ?
 =
 
 HCF × LCM
 30 × 1680

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let HCF = H

⇒ LCM = 56H

⇒ 56H + H = 1710

⇒ 57H = 1710

⇒ H = 1710 ÷ 57 = 30

⇒ HCF = 30

⇒ LCM = 56 × 30 = 1680

⇒ N₁ × N₂ = HCF × LCM

⇒ 240 × N₂ = 30 × 1680

⇒ N₂ = (30 × 1680) ÷ 240

⇒ N₂ = 30 × 7

⇒ N₂ = 210

**∴ The correct answer is 210.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Product of Two Numbers

For any two positive integers a and b, the product of the numbers is equal to the product of their HCF and LCM: a × b = HCF × LCM.

Co-prime Factors

If two numbers are expressed as H × x and H × y (where H is the HCF), then x and y are always co-prime to each other. Their LCM is formed by H × x × y.

LCM Divisibility

The LCM of a given set of numbers is always perfectly divisible by their HCF. Dividing the LCM by the HCF will always leave a remainder of 0.
</p

questions.question: A certain sum is deposited for 4 years at a rate of 10% per annum on compound interest compounded annually. The difference between the interest at the end of 2 years and that at the end of 4 years is Rs. 5,082. Find the sum (in Rs.).
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__**

We know, successive interest of a% and b% = [a + b + ab/100]%

The successive interest for 2 years = [10 + 10 + (10 × 10)/100]% = 21%

The successive interest for 3 years = [21 + 10 + (21 × 10)/100]% = 33.1%

The successive interest for 4 years = [33.1 + 10 + (33.1 × 10)/100]% = 46.41%

The difference of interest between 4 and 2 years = 46.41 - 21 = 25.41%

So, 25.41% → 5082

Then, 100% → (5082/25.41) × 100 = 20000

∴ The sum (in Rs.) is Rs. 20000

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

A certain sum is deposited for 4 years at a rate of 10% per annum on compound interest compounded annually.

Formula used:

At compound interest, the final amount = P(1+(r)/(100) )^n-P

Where, P = The sum of the amount

r = Rate of interest

n = Time (years)

**Calculation:**

Let, the sum of amount = x

[x(1+(10)/(100) )⁴-x]-[x(1+(10)/(100) )²-x] = 5082

⇒ [x((11)/(10) )⁴-x]-[x((11)/(10) )²-x] = 5082

⇒ (14641x)/(10000) - x - (121x)/(100) + x = 5082

⇒ 14641x/10000 - 121x/100 = 5082

⇒ 2541x/10000 = 5082

⇒ x = 5082 × (10000/2541) = 20000

**∴ The sum (in Rs.) is Rs. 20000**

questions.question: An equilateral triangle ABC is inscribed in a circle with centre O. D is a point on the minor arc BC and ∠CBD = 40º. Find the measure of ∠BCD.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

An equilateral triangle ABC is inscribed in a circle with centre O

∠CBD = 40º

**Concept used:**

The sum of the opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral = 180°

The sum of all three angles of a triangle = 180°

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/fd821fb8f9914d76aa4fd5516e519dcdbd19791178630913449618217285dcbc.png] 

∠ABC = ∠ACB = ∠BAC = 60° [∵ ΔABC is an equilateral triangle]

Also, ∠BAC + ∠BDC = 180°

⇒ 60° + ∠BDC = 180°

⇒ ∠BDC = 180° - 60° = 120°

Also, ∠CBD + ∠BDC + ∠BCD = 180°

⇒ 40° + 120° + ∠BCD = 180°

⇒ ∠BCD = 180° - 40° - 120° = 20°

**∴ The value of ∠BCD is 20°**

questions.question: The ratio of the monthly incomes of A and B is 11 : 13 and the ratio of their expenditures is 9 : 11. If both of them manage to save Rs. 4,000 per month, then find the difference in their incomes (in Rs.)
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Income ratio of A and B = 11 : 13

Expenditure ratio of A and B = 9 : 11

Since the difference between the ratio parts for both A and B is equal (11 − 9 = 2 and 13 − 11 = 2), these 2 units represent the savings directly.

2 units = ₹4,000

Difference in their incomes = 13 units − 11 units = 2 units

**∴ The correct answer is ₹4,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Income ratio of A and B = 11 : 13

Expenditure ratio of A and B = 9 : 11

Savings of both A and B = ₹4,000 each

 
 
 

 
 

 
 Income A = 11 units

 
 Income B = 13 units

 
 Exp. A = 9 units

 
 Exp. B = 11 units

 

 -2 units = ₹4000

 

 -2 units = ₹4000

**Formula Used:**

Income − Expenditure = Savings

**Calculations:**

Let the incomes of A and B be 11x and 13x respectively.

Let their expenditures be 9y and 11y respectively.

⇒ 11x − 9y = 4000 .... (i)

⇒ 13x − 11y = 4000 .... (ii)

Since both equal ₹4,000, we can equate equations (i) and (ii):

⇒ 11x − 9y = 13x − 11y

⇒ 11y − 9y = 13x − 11x

⇒ 2y = 2x

⇒ x = y

Substitute x = y in equation (i):

⇒ 11x − 9x = 4000

⇒ 2x = 4000

⇒ x = 2000

Now, to find the difference in their incomes:

⇒ Difference = 13x − 11x = 2x

⇒ Difference = 2 × 2000 = 4000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹4,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Income, Expenditure & Savings Relation

The foundational rule for all such problems is: Income = Expenditure + Savings. Any two known variables can be used to find the third.

Ratio Balancing Method

When the difference in ratio parts is not inherently equal across quantities, we balance the ratio gaps by multiplying the first ratio by the difference of the second ratio's terms, and vice versa.

Cross-Multiplication Trick

If an initial ratio a:b changes by quantities x and y to become c:d, then the value of 1 ratio unit can be evaluated instantly using |ad − bc| = |dx − cy|.

questions.question: A solid cube of side 8 cm is dropped into a rectangular container of length 16 cm, breadth 8 cm and height 15 cm which is partly filled with water. If the cube is completely submerged, then the rise of water level (in cm) is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Each side of the cube = 8 cm

The rectangular container has a length of 16 cm, breadth of 8 cm, and height of 15 cm

**Formula used:**

The volume of cube = (Edge)3

The volume of a cuboid = Length × Breadth × Height

**Calculation:**

The volume of cube = The volume of the rectangular container with a length of 16 cm, breadth of 8 cm, and height of the water level rise

Let, the height of the water level will rise = x cm

So, 8³ = 16 × 8 × x

⇒ 512 = 128 × x

⇒ x = 512/128 = 4

**∴ The rise of water level (in cm) is 4 cm**

questions.question: AB is a diameter of a circle with center O. A tangent is drawn at point A. C is a point on the circle such that BC produced meets the tangent at P. If ∠APC = 62º, then find the measure of the minor arc AC(i.e.∠ ABC).
questions.solution:
**Given:**

AB is a diameter of a circle with a center O

∠APC = 62º

**Concept used:**

The radius/diameter of a circle is always perpendicular to the tangent line.

Sum of all three angles of a triangle = 180°

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f83d6cac0e96deeb17665557a7bffb4be007e9849715da4d3ef4b61c6d476cec.png] 

Minor arc AC will create angle CBA

∠APC = 62º = ∠APB

∠BAP = 90° (diameter perpendicular to tangent)

In Δ APB,

∠APB + ∠BAP + ∠PBA = 180° 

⇒ ∠PBA = 180° - (90° + 62°)

⇒ ∠PBA = 28° 

**∴ The measure of minor arc AC is 28° **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e085a7f17645c801966c030eb44d69fae944b96fdb4c4077f5fba1bc2c24bc71.png] **__Mistake Points__**Measure of the minor arc AC is asked,

∠ABC marks arc AC, 

∴ ∠ABC is the correct angle to show a measure of arc AC

questions.question:
Monthly expenditure of a family on different heads is shown in the following pie chart.

The amount spent on Children Education, Transport and Rent is what percentage of the total earnings?

**Expenditure on different Heads**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/425540b2a9d3f84be4842a909e18388946ba7460e62a32e2c9a019d998ce0a03.png]
questions.solution:
**Given:**

There is the monthly expenditure of a family on different heads is shown in the following pie chart.

**Calculation:**

The total angle of all expenditures = 75° + 60° + 70° + 65° + 50° + 40° = 360°

The total angle of the amount spent on Children Education, Transport and Rent = 70° + 50° + 60° = 180°

The percentage = (180/360) × 100 = 50%

**∴ The amount spent on Children Education, Transport and Rent is 50% of the total earnings.**
